files.lesson.md: --- order: 10 unit: chance node: [AC9M8P01 n1, AC9M8P01 n2] uses: [AC9M7P01 n2] title: Complementary events summary: "An event and its complement (everything else that could happen) cover every outcome once. Use that to find probabilities quickly, especially for 'at least one'." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "The forecast says a 30% chance of rain. What is the chance it stays dry? You know straight away, but why does it work?" connection: chance-of-rain # data/connections/maths.yml (pilot: Make on paper and Also used in; documentation only) app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8328 url: http://127.0.0.1:8328/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: ev.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A dice: A is 'roll 1 or 2' (blue, 2 outcomes); not A is the other 4 (orange). 2/6 + 4/6 = 1." } explainClip: query: { code: "@ev.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "An event and its complement" say: "Every outcome is either in A, or in not A." clip: - caption: { text: "A: roll a 1 or a 2. P(A) = 2/6.", say: "Event A: roll a one or a two. Two out of six." } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "Not A: every other outcome, 3 to 6. P(not A) = 4/6.", say: "Not A is everything else: four out of six." } - click: Show not A - expect: { selector: "#gnote", contains: "P(A) + P(not A) = 1" } - caption: { text: "Together they cover every outcome once: 2/6 + 4/6 = 1.", say: "Together they make one." } - wait: 1600 --- An **event** is a set of outcomes, such as "roll a 5 or a 6". ## Predict: not red ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to P(not red) from P(red) alone shows whether they see that the other colours don't need to be known." check: type: predict q: "A spinner lands on red with probability 0.35. It has other colours too. What is the probability it does not land on red?" options: ["You need to know the other colours", "0.65", "0.35"] actual: "0.65. Not red is every other outcome, so P(not red) = 1 − 0.35, whatever the other colours are." ``` ## Run: an event and its complement ```step stage: run insight: "Choosing an event on a dice and showing its complement shows the two cover every outcome once, so their probabilities add to 1." try: { playground: board, starter: "ev.yml#run", height: 520 } check: { type: board, text: "Click the outcomes for A: 'roll at least 5'. Then press Show not A. Do P(A) and P(not A) add to 1? Does that match your prediction?", when: "r = 1 and k = 1", explain: "P(A) = 2/6 and P(not A) = 4/6. Every outcome is in exactly one of them, so they add to 1." } ``` The **complement** of an event A, written **not A** (or A′), is every other outcome in the sample space. Every outcome is in A or in not A, never both and never neither. So: $$P(A) + P(\text{not } A) = 1 \qquad P(\text{not } A) = 1 - P(A)$$ ## Investigate: using the complement ```step stage: investigate insight: "Subtract from 1 to find a complement; events that can't happen together are not always complementary (Ben); a complementary pair must cover every outcome." tasks: - check: type: number q: "The chance a bus is late is 0.15. What is the chance it is not late?" answer: 0.85 tolerance: 0.001 feedback: - ["0.15", "That is the chance it is late. Not late is everything else: 1 − 0.15."] explain: "P(not late) = 1 − 0.15 = 0.85." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ben" text: "Ben works with two events on a dice. Click the line where his reasoning goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: complement-exclusive explain: "Line 3: A and B can't happen together, but they don't cover every outcome (2, 3, 4 and 5 are in neither). Complementary events must cover everything. P(B) = 1/6." - check: type: question q: "On one roll of a dice, which pair of events is complementary?" options: ["Roll more than 3; roll less than 3", "Roll a 6; roll a 5 or a 6", "Roll an even number; roll an odd number", "Roll a 1; roll a 6"] answer: 2 feedback: ["3 is in neither.", "These overlap: 6 is in both.", null, "2, 3, 4 and 5 are in neither."] explain: "Every number is even or odd, never both: together they cover every outcome once." ``` ### Not late Here is the routine. ```worked P(\text{red}) = \tfrac{3}{8} :: A bag has 3 red counters out of 8. P(\text{not red}) = 1 - \tfrac{3}{8} :: Not red is every other counter. = \tfrac{5}{8} :: Check: 5 counters are not red. ``` ### Find the mistake Read Ben's working. Which outcomes are in neither event? ### Which pair ## Modify: at least one ```step stage: modify insight: "'At least one six' has many cases, but its complement 'no six' is one block: count it and subtract." try: { playground: board, starter: "ev.yml#nosix", height: 640 } tasks: - starter: "ev.yml#nosix" hint: ["No six means the first dice is not 6 and the second is not 6.", "That is the 5 by 5 block of outcomes from 1 to 5. Clicking a row or column number chooses the whole row or column."] check: { type: board, text: "Two dice are rolled. Choose every outcome with no six at all.", when: "r = 1", explain: "25 outcomes: both dice show 1 to 5." } - check: type: answer q: "So what is the probability of at least one six when two dice are rolled?" answer: "11/36" feedback: - ["12/36", "Six with the first dice plus six with the second counts (6, 6) twice."] - ["25/36", "That is the chance of no six. At least one six is the complement."] explain: "At least one six is the complement of no six: 1 − 25/36 = 11/36." - check: type: question q: "Three coins are tossed. What is the probability of at least one head?" options: ["7/8", "1/8", "3/8", "1/2"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That is the chance of no heads (TTT).", "That is exactly one head.", "Count the 8 outcomes: only TTT has no head."] explain: "Only TTT has no heads, so P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8." smaller: check: { type: number, q: "Three coins make 8 outcomes, from HHH to TTT. How many of them have no heads at all?", answer: 1, tolerance: 0, feedback: [[0, "Look at TTT."], [3, "That's the outcomes with exactly one head. We want none."]], explain: "Only TTT has no heads. One outcome out of 8." } - check: type: number q: "A factory finds that 2% of its light globes are faulty. What percentage are not faulty?" answer: 98 tolerance: 0 explain: "100% − 2% = 98%: probabilities as percentages add to 100%." ``` ### No six ### At least one six ### Three coins ### Faulty globes ## Practise: complements ```step stage: practise insight: "Complements in decimals, fractions, percentages and words, mixed; calling events that can't happen together complementary is the planted slip; expected count is the Year 7 review." tasks: - check: type: number q: "P(a team wins) = 0.45. A draw is not possible. What is P(the team does not win)?" answer: 0.55 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "1 − 0.45 = 0.55." - check: type: question q: "On a dice, what is the complement of 'roll at least 4'?" options: ["Roll 3 or less", "Roll less than 4 or more than 4", "Roll a 4", "Roll more than 4"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "More than 4 is part of 'at least 4'.", "4 is in the event itself.", "That is part of the event."] explain: "At least 4 is 4, 5, 6, so the complement is 1, 2, 3." - check: type: question q: "A card is drawn from a pack. A is 'a heart' and B is 'a spade'. Are A and B complementary?" options: ["Yes: they can't both happen", "Yes: they are both suits", "No: they can both happen", "No: some cards are in neither"] answer: 3 feedback: ["Not happening together is not enough: they must cover every card.", "Clubs and diamonds are missing.", "A heart and a spade can't be drawn at once.", null] explain: "They can't both happen, but clubs and diamonds are in neither. Complementary events cover every outcome: P(not a heart) = 3/4, not P(spade)." - check: type: number q: "Review: a dice is rolled 120 times. How many sixes do you expect?" answer: 20 tolerance: 0 explain: "1/6 × 120 = 20." ``` ### Win or not ### Complement in words ### Cards ### Review: expected count ## Make: a quarter ```step stage: make insight: "Building an event with a given probability, then its complement, shows they can reason from P to outcomes." try: { playground: board, starter: "ev.yml#make", height: 640 } hint: ["P(A) = 1/4 means 9 of the 36 outcomes.", "Try a rule, such as 'the first dice is even and the second is 3 or less'. Clicking a row number chooses a whole row."] check: { type: board, text: "Two dice: choose an event A with P(A) = 1/4. Then show not A. What is P(not A)?", when: "n = 9 and k = 1", explain: "Any 9 outcomes give 9/36 = 1/4, and not A is the other 27: P(not A) = 3/4." } ``` Then describe your event in words, so someone else could check it. ## Make: a forecast on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A rain forecast needs the complement to turn into days; the paper task makes them state why P(dry) = 1 - P(rain) and use it." hint: ["Dry is the complement of rain.", "30% of 40 days are wet."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The forecast says a 30% chance of rain on each school day for the next 40 school days. If the forecasts are right, about how many of those days will be dry?" steps: - ["$P(\\text{rain}) = 0.3$", "30% as a decimal"] - ["$P(\\text{dry}) = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7$", "rain and dry cover every outcome once"] - ["$0.7 \\times 40 = 28$ days", "about 28 dry days"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Why is the chance of a dry day 1 − 0.3?" options: - "Rain and dry together cover every outcome exactly once, so their chances add to 1" - "Dry days never overlap with sunny days" - "The forecaster always rounds up" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Think about a day that is neither rain nor dry. Is there one?", "The forecast is not rounded up. The two chances simply add to 1."] answer: "28" feedback: - ["12", "That is the number of wet days. The question asks for the dry ones."] - ["0.7", "That is the chance of one dry day, not the number of days."] criteria: - "I wrote P(rain) and P(dry) so they add to 1." - "I used the complement, not the other colours or days." - "My answer is about 28, and I said 'about'." explain: "P(dry) = 1 − 0.3 = 0.7, and 0.7 × 40 = 28. Rain here means any rain at all, so a wet day can be a light shower." ``` Do this one in your book. The 40 days are made up, but a real school can check the forecast against a term of rain. Write the complement first, then the number of days, and type the dry days. **Also used in** - **Forecasts.** The chance of rain is the chance of any rain at all. The complement is the chance of staying dry. - **Camps.** A three-day camp with a 30% chance of rain each day is easiest to answer by finding the chance of no rain at all and taking it from 1. You will meet that in Year 10. - **Games.** A 1-in-8 bonus spin is a 7-in-8 ordinary spin. ```teacher summary: Students choose events on a dice and two dice, show their complements, and use P(not A) = 1 − P(A), including for 'at least one' (AC9M8P01, nodes 1 and 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can name the complement of an event. - I can find P(not A) from P(A), in fractions, decimals and percentages. - I can use the complement to find the chance of 'at least one'. struggle: "Telling complementary from 'can't happen together'. Ask: does every outcome land in one of the two?" before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need sample spaces and probability as a fraction (Year 7 Chance). The one idea: an event and its complement cover every outcome exactly once, so their probabilities add to 1. The common mistake is calling any two events that can't happen together complementary (Ben's mistake); complementary events must also cover everything. "Mutually exclusive" is the formal word for can't-happen-together; it is used in the teacher notes, not required of students yet. 'At least one' is the main use: one block to count (none) instead of many cases. Wider: the chance of at least one six in four rolls of a dice, 1 − (5/6)⁴, a famous gambling question (needs multiplying, Year 10). running: - "Predict: ask whether the other colours matter." - "Run: ask whether any outcome is in both, or in neither." - "Investigate: ask Ben where a roll of 3 goes." - "Modify: ask why counting 'no six' is quicker than 'at least one six'." - "Make: ask how many outcomes make a quarter of 36." - "Paper: the forecast task is worked in books; the page marks the number of dry days and the reason for 1 − 0.3. Books out, then ask if anyone found the wet days first and subtracted." stuck: - see: A student says a heart and a spade are complementary. ask: Where do clubs go? fix: Complementary events cover every outcome. - see: A student counts 12 outcomes with at least one six. ask: Which outcome did you count twice? fix: (6, 6) is in both rows; or count no six (25) and subtract from 36. - see: A student writes P(not A) = P(A). ask: Which outcomes are not in A? fix: Count everything else, or subtract from 1. stretch: "Two dice are rolled. Which is more likely: at least one six, or a sum of 7 or more? Use complements." support: A sample space printed as a grid, with two colours of highlighter. leads: > This covers AC9M8P01. Where it leads: two-way tables and Venn diagrams (next), and 'and', 'or' and 'not' in compound events. exit: q: "P(it snows tomorrow) = 0.08. What is P(it does not snow)? Then: two coins are tossed; what is P(at least one tail)?" a: 0.92. And 1 − P(HH) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4. explain: > The **complement** of an event A, written **not A**, is every other outcome. A and not A cover every outcome exactly once, so **P(A) + P(not A) = 1**, and P(not A) = 1 − P(A). This makes **at least one** easy: count the outcomes with none, and subtract from 1. Two events that just can't happen together are not complementary unless they cover every outcome too. ```

files.working.txt:
# Ben's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: ben
Ben rolls a dice. Event A is "roll a 1" and event B is "roll a 6".
A and B cannot both happen on the same roll.
So A and B are complementary events.
So P(B) = 1 − P(A) = 1 − 1/6 = 5/6.
# endregion
